_source: holdouts/regroup.py, 21 November 2026. Families of the undecided holdouts (standing open, cryptid or pr on the index) that one proof technique could settle together; ranked R01 first. 'set' is the table set (single-linkage at table distance <= 1 up to renaming and mirror; T1 is the largest, and table_sets names each by its smallest member); 'old' is the 13 November family; 'pending' are the machines whose only proof is an uncompiled outside pull request.

families.name: Base-5 marker counter on one five-state core (F05)
families.mechanism: Forty machines are one five-state core, `1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE?LF_1LA0LB_??---` in frame A, differing in D1, F0 and the start; five more use the same core with E1 or F0 changed. The tape is a list of 0010-blocks run like a nested base-5 counter; a machine can halt only at an F-event (the detour through F) that reads a 1.
families.known: Lean proves the visit law, its closed form and a conservation law for all 40 on each machine's own table (`Family.lean` in each folder); the exact block-list map ran 37 of them to 10^200 steps, every F-event reading 0. The same-run step is done: ten twin pairs and seven start-twin pairs (`EQUIVALENCES.md`; `Twin.lean`, `StartTwin.lean`) put 31 of the 40 into 14 classes, so the 40 are 23 questions, and a recheck of all 40 block lists at every left-end event to 10^30 steps (21 November) found no further pair: the twelve start-E machines part from each other and from the start-A ones by the sixth left-end event.
families.technique: One invariant on the shared core: show that an F-event never reads 1, i.e. that the drift b(i+1) - 5·b(i) is never within a few hundred of 0 when block i runs out. Clean visits keep every drift fixed, so only the drifts made at merges matter. A proof on the core settles all 40 at once.
families.odds: low: the drifts made at merges behave like differences of unrelated large numbers. To 10^100 steps the 599 drifts of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE0LF_1LA0LB_0RA--- are all even but take every residue mod 9 and mod 25 (122 of 125 mod 125), and |b(i+1) - 5·b(i)| / b(i) gets as low as 0.015, so neither a congruence nor a ratio bound is kept. A proof would have to show that a chaotic integer process misses a thin set, a Collatz-type statement. Heuristically they do not halt: every drift made after the 30th left-end event is above 8·10^6 in size, against the few hundred a halt needs.
families.short: one drift invariant on the shared core (same-run step done: 40 machines, 23 questions)

families.name: Clock and word: a block grows in doubling time while a word map runs 2^k times
families.mechanism: A block at one end grows by 2, 3 or 4 cells per tick and tick k applies one word map P (one trip of the head) 2^k times to the word beside it; halting is possible only when a rebuild of the end goes wrong. Six tables.
families.known: The clock lemma (block growth and the 2^k trips, whenever the trips return) is proved in Lean for every k on six of them, for example `1RB0RA_1RC0RC_1LD0LE_1RA1LC_1LC0LF_0LC---` and `1RB---_1RC1RF_1LD1RE_1LB1LD_0RB0RC_1RA0LF`. DeepMind's file lists three as cryptids. Since 21 Nov: 12 of the 15 run on these six tables, the clock is in Lean for all 12 and the exact accelerated simulator covers them all (no halt; T20 and T45 members past 10^162 to 10^202 steps). See `R02-clock-word/README.md`.
families.technique: Close the word map alone: find a regular language of words that P maps into itself and that never triggers the halting rebuild (a SAT search over automata on the word, much smaller than the whole-tape search that failed in `satctl.json`), then combine it with the clock lemma in Lean. The same pipeline serves every member; only P changes. (21 Nov: P fails at every phase end, so the word map cannot be closed alone; generic words make a phase end halt on four of the six tables, never on T88, where an invariant that forgets the word is being searched with `tools/py/satctl_forget.py`.)
families.odds: medium: the remaining question is one finite-state map per machine, not a counter race; the three DeepMind cryptids are the least likely.
families.short: automaton invariant for the word map P alone, plus the clock lemma in Lean

families.name: Blocks of 10s split by 01100: one table core with cursors that triple blocks
families.mechanism: Twelve machines one transition apart (tracker class Chaotic Bell Class 3) and three neighbours two transitions away: a list of blocks (10)^n separated by 01100 or single 1s, with a cursor or reflector that walks through it and triples or moves blocks, on a budget held in the first block.
families.known: Round trips and the moving reflector are proved in Lean for several, for example `1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RD1LF_0LA---` and `1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RD1LF_0LC---`; `1RB1RF_1RC0RE_1LD0RB_1RE0LC_1RA0LE_0RC---` has a halting tape of the same form proved in Lean.
families.technique: Do for this core what `Family.lean` did for F05: one generated Lean library of the shared rules proved on every member's table, then an exact block-list map per member run far to hunt for halts (the budget rules make a halt plausible).
families.odds: medium: shared rules make the library cheap; whether the runs halt is unknown.
families.short: shared Lean library for the core, then exact block-list runs to hunt halts

families.name: Base-4 counters with countdown timers (Skelet 1-like)
families.mechanism: A base-4 counter whose digits sit between blocks, and blocks that lose 4^i (or 9, 24, 96, ...) units per visit like timers; when a timer runs out digits fuse or a level is rebuilt.
families.known: Digit and sweep rules are proved in Lean for several; for `1RB1RE_1LC0RC_1RA1LD_1RB0LA_0LC1RF_---1RD` and `1RB1RE_1LC0RF_1LA0LD_1LE1LC_0RA0LC_1RA---` Lean proves that tapes of the same shape with short timers halt. `1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD` halts iff its twin `1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE` halts from state B (Lean). `1RB0RB_0LC1RA_1RD1LC_1LA1LE_1LF0LD_---0LA` was decided by busycoq PR 64 (halts; compiled here 21 November).
families.technique: Halt hunting with exact odometer jumps (the PR 83 / PR 89 method: b^k ticks in one operation, then an exact executor to the halt). In the week of 13 November this kind of family (F06) gave half of all decisions, all of them halting.
families.odds: medium-high for halts: short-timer tapes halt, so a run that reaches one is a proof.
families.short: halt hunting with exact odometer jumps (PR 83 / 89 method)

families.name: Cellular-automaton sweeps: running parity and Sierpinski triangles
families.mechanism: Each sweep rewrites the tape like one step of a one-dimensional cellular automaton. In `1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF` and its slower twin `1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF` a leftward sweep replaces a binary word by its running parity, so the space-time diagram is Pascal's triangle mod 2; `1RB1LB_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LE0LA_---0RB` runs rule 102 (XOR); the others draw Sierpinski-like triangles on blocks of 1s.
families.known: Lean proves for `1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF` (and, renamed, `1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF`) that one bounce maps the zone to the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2 for every zone word, solves the rows by Lucas' theorem, and that a right turn at a frozen block of odd length halts whatever the zone; so halting depends on the parities of the frozen blocks, not on the zone's digits. At every right turn of the four runs on that table (10^10 steps for the first, 10^9 for the others) the tape right of the head is a word in the 2-cell letters 11, 01, which rules that out (observed, not proved). Two pairs run through the same tapes (observed); for the XOR machine the bulk-merge trigger is known and was last seen at 4.07·10^6 steps in a 10^11 run.
families.technique: For the parity machines, prove in Lean that sweep n writes row n of Pascal's triangle mod 2 in 4-cell letters. Lucas' theorem then gives every cell in closed form, and the halting condition becomes a statement about binary digits that may be provable outright. The same template (sweep = one CA step, then a closed form of the CA) is the route for the rest.
families.odds: medium for the parity pair, low for the others; untried, and a closed form is rare among holdouts.
families.short: prove each sweep is one CA step; closed form by Lucas' theorem for the parity pair

families.name: Neighbours of DeepMind's PR 93 tables (the T3 and T4 engine)
families.mechanism: Eleven open machines within one transition of the PR 93 tables, whose five decided members all halt (PR 93, PR 100, PR 102, and our 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- and 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LE). Behaviour varies: chaotic bells over runs 1^(6k+1), sweeping transducers, counters with long digits.
families.known: `1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF` runs 10^1336 steps without a halt on the PR 93 engine, with a Coq skeleton that compiles and waits only for the engine to stop.
families.technique: Retarget the PR 93 run-length engine (each rule proved sound) to every member and run it to the halt. It can prove halting only; a member that does not halt needs a different argument.
families.odds: medium: five of sixteen in this neighbourhood halted this way, but the remaining runs are already long.
families.short: retarget the PR 93 engine and run to the halt (halting only)

families.name: Up/down counters and two binary counters with rebuilds
families.mechanism: One counter counts up while another counts down; when the down counter is empty a rebuild eats low digits of the other and refills it. A halt needs one exact rebuild (for example a walk that crosses the whole counter).
families.known: Ticks are proved in Lean for every size; the rebuilds are known in closed form (checked, not proved) and iterated past 10^150,000,000 steps. Two former members were decided by outside non-halting proofs compiled here on 21 November: busycoq PR 57 (`1RB1LE_1RC0RB_1LD1RC_1LA1LE_1LF0LA_1LC---`) and PR 58 (`1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC`); their wall invariants are the model for the rest.
families.technique: Prove the closed rebuild recursions in Lean and extend the PR 57/58 wall invariant to the case where a rebuild reads only part of the counter (that is where it failed for the three siblings).
families.odds: medium: the rebuilds are already explicit maps; the last step is a number-theoretic inequality.
families.short: prove the closed rebuild maps; extend the PR 57/58 wall invariant

families.name: Reservoir counters: a chaotic zone eats a reservoir behind a growing block
families.mechanism: A block of words grows at one end; behind it a zone of about a hundred cells is rewritten like a counter and slowly eats a reservoir; the far end is touched at rare events, and only those can halt.
families.known: Lean proves the halting pattern for the four 111110-machines; a model of their leftmost zone reproduces every real arrival at the left end. For `1RB1RC_1LC0RE_1LD0LB_1RA1LC_1RA1RF_---1RD` the reservoir is decoded as independent mod-4 counters and Lean proves a halt can only happen beyond the far end.
families.technique: Prove the leftmost-zone reduction in Lean (the 16 November plan's item 3), then model two zones with the block between them. Could settle the four 111110-machines either way, and the same tools apply to the five reservoir eaters.
families.odds: medium for the four, low for the rest (their next events are 2^1100 sweeps away or more).
families.short: Lean leftmost-zone reduction, then a two-zone model

families.name: Word map phi with a counter: one table, a race between word and collisions
families.mechanism: Six machines are one table with A1, F0 or the start changed (plus a separator counter one transition away, `1RB---_1RC0RD_1RD1RA_1LE1RB_0LF0LE_1RF0RD`): a binary counter applies a word map phi twice per step, and anomalies and collision cascades rewrite the word.
families.known: For `1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---` every macro step is proved in Lean as one map on word-and-counter configurations, and Lean proves the machine never halts if that map never fails; it does not fail in 10^8 macro steps.
families.technique: Port the one-map reduction to the five siblings (same table, so the rules carry over), then look for an invariant of the map. A failure found by running the map would be a halting proof for all members with the same run.
families.odds: medium-low: the race looks Collatz-like, but the reduction already exists.
families.short: port the one-map reduction to the siblings; invariant of the map

families.name: Visit laws on streams (busycoq PR 59 family)
families.mechanism: Two binary counters off one engine, read as a rewriting system on streams; the first four rules are those of the PR 59 machines.
families.known: Busycoq PR 59 claims halting for `1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---`, `1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC---` and `1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---`, and PR 55 non-halting for `1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---`; all four compiled here on 21 November, so they are decided. The three open members rewrite 1011 differently and run past round 200,000 (visit law in Lean).
families.technique: For the three open members, continue the accelerated visit-law run: our two halting proofs from 13 November came from this law.
families.short: accelerated visit-law runs (PRs 55 and 59 compiled: four decided)

families.name: Nested ternary counters (draining odometers)
families.mechanism: Segments of 111-blocks (or digits between blocks) drained by 3^j per event; segments run out one after another and the counter settles into a new regime.
families.known: Every rule of `1RB0RF_1LC1RF_1RA0LD_0LC0RE_1LD---_0RC0RD` and `1RB1RF_1LC0RE_1RD0LC_0LB0RA_1LD1RD_1RB---` is proved in Lean; `1RB1RF_1LC0RE_1RD0LC_0LB0RA_1LD1RD_1RB---` passes round 33,199,619 without a halt, its next event about 2.7·10^12 rounds out.
families.technique: Exact macro simulators to the first top-level overflow (halt hunting), as for R04.
families.short: exact macro simulators to the first top-level overflow

families.name: Two-word sweepers: base-3 and binary counters side by side
families.mechanism: A base-3 counter and binary counters fed by one engine; overflows shift the layout and pile junk into an undecoded middle.
families.known: The counters are proved in Lean for every size; DeepMind's file classes most of them as cryptids.
families.technique: Decode the middle first; no multi-machine proof is in sight.

families.name: Shifted-run quartet (F09)
families.mechanism: Four tables one transition apart whose runs are one shifted run (observed to 2·10^12 steps): an exact ternary counter whose digits are pairs of long alternating runs read mod 4.
families.known: The increment and the shuttle are proved in Lean for `1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---`; `1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE---` has its own folder (`bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB`).
families.technique: A transfer theory for the shifted run would settle the four at once.
families.short: transfer theory for the shifted run

families.name: Block lists rewritten like a cellular automaton (blocks of 4k+3 ones)
families.mechanism: Bouncers whose tape is a list of numbers written as blocks of 4k+3 ones (or a dense and a sparse form), rewritten chaotically on every round trip.
families.technique: None yet; park unless R05 finds a usable closed form.

families.name: Collatz-like maps and cryptids (parked)
families.mechanism: The run is (provably, for many) the orbit of an explicit Collatz-like map: 3/2 and 4/3 growth with a parity- or residue-driven counter (Antihydra-like), doubling maps modulo a growing number, Euclid-like two-counter games, halving cascades.
families.known: Lean proves `halts_iff` for an explicit map for many of them (the index's 'proved map' column); DeepMind's file has a map or a cryptid label for most.
families.technique: No proof technique applies: these are open number-theory questions. Only halting can be decided, by running the proved maps far with big integers when the map is 'probviously halting'.
families.odds: very low for non-halting; occasional halts.
families.short: halt hunts on proved maps only

families.name: Outside proofs awaiting compilation (busycoq PR 60)
families.technique: Compiled on 21 November 2026 (`tools/coq/busycoq/prs-43-68`): every machine proof in PRs 43 to 68 compiles and 32 machines moved to decided. Left: the two halts of PR 60, whose proofs are about 275 and 280 core-hours of native_compute jobs; sample jobs pass here, the full runs need a large machine.
families.short: compile and record; listed here are the 1 with no other family, the other 1 pending machines sit in R15
